summary: Remove code2llm Shotgun Surgery: cmd smell (PLF-039) by consolidating healing-webhook argv construction into one _build_command helper

delivery.outcome: services/healing-webhook/app.py assembles every subprocess argv through one _build_command helper, removing the code2llm Shotgun Surgery: cmd smell (planfile PLF-039).
nonGoals: Sibling smells in the same file (payload/proc/outcome) tracked by separate planfile tickets
Behaviour or argv-shape changes to any healing strategy

architecture.decision: Add a module-level _build_command(base, *flags) helper as the single owner of argv plus conditional flag assembly in services/healing-webhook/app.py; route the planfile, docker (redsl/rebuild), vallm and redup call sites through it so no function builds and mutates its own cmd list.
architecture.rollback: Revert the single ticket commit; every call site returns to its previous inline argv list with no cross-function coupling.

validation.evidence: New tests cover _build_command base/flag-bundle/None handling (including base-list copy semantics) and _build_planfile_command label assembly.
Pre-existing test_run_docker_uses_expected_command still asserts the exact docker argv; the refactor only changes where argv lists are assembled.

commands:
python3 - <<'PY'
from code2llm.core.config import Config
from code2llm.core.analyzer import ProjectAnalyzer
result = ProjectAnalyzer(Config()).analyze_project('services/healing-webhook')
assert not [s for s in result.smells if s.type == 'shotgun_surgery' and s.context.get('variable') == 'cmd']
PY
validation.evidence: code2llm ProjectAnalyzer over the services/healing-webhook package reports no shotgun_surgery smell for variable cmd after the consolidation.
